answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying reputation to verifiable work history instead of a fresh account. Each agent carries a signed ledger of completed jobs, peer endorsements, and staked collateral, so a new identity starts with no plume of trust and no haven in high-value trades. Copying a real agent's record is a fable: signatures won't match, and one bad job burns the stake. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs real collateral and time, while honest agents earn access cheaply.
